pages.title: About
pages.content:
About

SINCE 2014

Home / About

About

Founded in 2014, Yawara Rheumatology provides structured diagnostic care and long-term joint management in Harrow Quay. We organize our clinic around the morning hours when inflammatory symptoms are most pronounced.

A clinic built around the morning

Dr. Miriam Achterberg established Yawara Rheumatology in 2014 after spending eleven years working within a busy hospital rheumatology unit. During those hospital years, she observed that patients frequently had to explain their worst morning stiffness in the middle of an afternoon appointment, long after early symptoms had temporarily receded. Our clinic at 12 Linden Row was intentionally organized to address that gap. We open at 8:30 each morning to evaluate joints when inflammation is active and measurable. By aligning clinical schedules with the natural rhythm of inflammatory disease, we gather accurate diagnostic information and help patients maintain their daily routines.

Why we examine twenty-eight joints

At every comprehensive consultation and routine review, our clinicians perform a standardized examination of twenty-eight individual joints. Rather than inspecting only the single knuckle or wrist that prompted your visit, we assess both hands, wrists, elbows, shoulders, knees, and ankles. This systematic count monitors subtle swelling, joint tenderness, and warmth across your body over time. Standardized joint scores remove guesswork from treatment decisions, allowing us to see whether inflammation is spreading, stabilizing, or receding under current therapy. Recording twenty-eight distinct points creates an objective clinical record that guides treatment adjustments across months and years.

Hand care

OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY

Why every patient receives a written plan

Long-term joint care requires total clarity between patient and clinician. Following your initial assessment and diagnostic investigations, we hold a dedicated plan meeting within ten days to agree on a one-page written management plan. This single sheet outlines your diagnosis, prescribed medications, scheduled review intervals, physical therapy goals, and emergency contact steps. Both the rheumatologist and the patient sign this document, ensuring mutual agreement on every step. Having a clear written record eliminates confusion, coordinates care with your named nurse, and gives you a dependable reference whenever symptoms shift.

pages.title: Conditions
pages.content:
Conditions

WHERE TO START

Home / Conditions

Conditions

We provide diagnostic evaluation and ongoing medical management for six primary inflammatory rheumatic conditions. Early assessment helps protect joint function and reduces morning stiffness before long-term structural changes occur.

Rheumatoid arthritis

WHAT WE CHECK

Rheumatoid arthritis

Rheumatoid arthritis typically presents as persistent symmetrical swelling, heat, and stiffness in the small joints of the hands and feet. Morning stiffness often lasts well past breakfast, making everyday tasks difficult before midday. During your assessment, we conduct a twenty-eight joint examination, perform bedside ultrasound to identify active synovial inflammation, and check inflammatory blood markers. General practitioners commonly refer patients to our Harrow Quay clinic when hand joints remain swollen for more than several weeks, allowing us to initiate disease-modifying treatment without unnecessary delay.

Psoriatic arthritis

Psoriatic arthritis causes inflammation in the joints and surrounding tendons, frequently affecting individuals with current or past skin psoriasis. Patients often notice swollen, sausage-like fingers or toes, Achilles tendon tenderness, lower back stiffness, and pitted fingernails. We inspect peripheral joints, evaluate enthesitis sites where tendons attach to bone, and utilize ultrasound imaging to examine inflamed tendon sheaths. Referrals arrive from dermatologists and family physicians who observe joint pain developing alongside skin changes, ensuring both dermatological and rheumatological aspects receive balanced clinical attention.

Gout

WHAT WE CHECK

Gout

Gout is an intensely painful inflammatory arthritis triggered by the accumulation of urate crystals within joint spaces. Attacks typically begin suddenly overnight, leaving a single joint—often the big toe, ankle, or knee—severely swollen, red, hot, and sensitive to light touch. We check serum uric acid levels, assess joint fluid when appropriate, and use ultrasound to detect crystal deposition along cartilage surfaces. General practitioners refer patients experiencing recurrent sudden flares or persistent joint discomfort to establish effective long-term urate-lowering strategies.

Axial spondyloarthritis

Axial spondyloarthritis affects the spine and sacroiliac joints, causing persistent inflammatory lower back pain and morning stiffness that improves with physical movement rather than rest. Patients frequently wake during the second half of the night with spinal discomfort and experience deep buttock pain. Our clinic checks spinal mobility measurements, screens for HLA-B27 genetic markers, and arranges targeted magnetic resonance imaging of sacroiliac joints. Physiotherapists and family doctors routinely refer younger adults experiencing chronic nocturnal back stiffness that has persisted for months.

Moving well

PHYSIOTHERAPY

Polymyalgia rheumatica

Polymyalgia rheumatica presents with sudden, severe stiffness and aching across the shoulder girdle, neck, and pelvic hips, predominantly in adults over fifty. Getting out of bed, putting on a jacket, or combing hair in the morning becomes difficult and painful. We assess functional mobility, verify rapid responses to targeted anti-inflammatory regimens, and measure erythrocyte sedimentation rates and C-reactive protein. Family practitioners refer patients promptly to confirm the diagnosis and rule out concurrent giant cell arteritis through careful clinical evaluation.

Systemic lupus erythematosus

Systemic lupus erythematosus, commonly known as lupus or SLE, is a complex autoimmune condition affecting joints, skin, kidneys, and blood cells. Symptoms can include joint aches with morning swelling, butterfly facial rashes, extreme fatigue, sun sensitivity, and pleuritic chest pain. We perform comprehensive serological testing for antinuclear antibodies, anti-double-stranded DNA, and complement levels, alongside urine protein analysis. Community physicians refer individuals presenting with multifaceted symptoms across different organ systems for specialist diagnostic confirmation and ongoing monitoring.

pages.title: Your first visit
pages.content:
Your first visit

FIRST VISIT

Home / Your first visit

Your first visit

A thorough initial consultation allows us to understand your symptoms, establish an accurate diagnosis, and agree on a clear path forward. We dedicate sixty minutes to your first appointment at our Harrow Quay clinic.

Diary sheet printable

Seven mornings

THE DIARY

Call and seven-day morning stiffness diary

Before attending your first appointment, you begin by contacting our reception desk to register your details. We immediately provide a printable seven-day morning stiffness diary sheet. Over the course of one full week, you record the exact time your joints feel stiff upon waking, how long that stiffness takes to ease, and which specific joints feel warm or swollen each day. Bringing this completed diary sheet to your appointment gives your rheumatologist an objective record of your daily symptom pattern, ensuring we do not rely solely on how your joints feel on appointment day.

Room 2

ULTRASOUND ON THE DAY

Ultrasound room / 8:40

The sixty-minute comprehensive consultation

Your sixty-minute initial consultation includes an in-depth clinical history, a standardized twenty-eight joint examination, and diagnostic joint ultrasound performed during the visit. Dr. Miriam Achterberg or Dr. Kofi Mensah-Lund evaluates each joint for swelling, tenderness, and range of movement. Bedside ultrasound allows us to visualize joint lining inflammation and fluid accumulation beneath the skin immediately. Blood samples for inflammatory markers and autoantibodies are collected on-site the same morning. This thorough diagnostic approach ensures all primary clinical investigations are completed within a single morning appointment without repeated hospital visits.

Plan meeting within ten days

Within ten days of your first appointment, you return to the clinic for a dedicated thirty-minute plan meeting. During this session, your rheumatologist reviews your blood results, ultrasound images, and physical findings with you. Together, we formulate a single-page written management plan that outlines your diagnosis, medical prescriptions, physiotherapy recommendations, and scheduled review milestones. Both you and your doctor sign this sheet, and a copy is placed in your hands. This agreement provides clear direction and shared expectations right from the start of your medical care.

Scheduled reviews and your named nurse

Ongoing care follows an agreed review timetable at four, twelve, and twenty-four weeks, progressing to regular check-ups every three months once symptoms stabilize. Each review repeats the twenty-eight joint count to track objective changes over time. Between scheduled visits, every registered patient has direct access to our named rheumatology nurse specialist line, managed by Ines Varga. You can call with questions regarding medication tolerability or symptom changes without waiting for your next appointment, ensuring consistent clinical support whenever you need reassurance.

+1 555 0142 300

Mon–Fri 8:30–17:30 · Sat 8:30–12:30 · Closed Sun & public holidays

pages.title: Team
pages.content:
Team

THE TEAM

Home / Team

Team

Our multidisciplinary team brings together clinical rheumatologists, specialist nurses, therapists, and administrative staff at 12 Linden Row. Every member coordinates closely to support your joint health and daily function.

Miriam Achterberg

LEAD RHEUMATOLOGIST

Ines Varga

NURSE SPECIALIST

Tamsin Rehn

PHYSIOTHERAPIST

Dr. Miriam Achterberg

Founder, lead rheumatologist

Dr. Miriam Achterberg is the founder and lead rheumatologist at Yawara Rheumatology. She established the Harrow Quay practice in 2014 following eleven years of clinical practice within a hospital rheumatology department. Dr. Achterberg specializes in early inflammatory arthritis, standardized twenty-eight joint assessments, and patient-agreed written management plans. Her clinical work focuses on diagnosing morning stiffness promptly so patients can retain mobility and protect long-term joint function throughout their daily lives.

Dr. Kofi Mensah-Lund

Rheumatologist, musculoskeletal ultrasound

Dr. Kofi Mensah-Lund is a consultant rheumatologist specializing in musculoskeletal ultrasound imaging and diagnostic joint assessments. He performs bedside sonography during initial consultations to detect early synovial thickening, active joint effusion, and tendon inflammation. Dr. Mensah-Lund collaborates closely with patients during first visits and follow-up reviews to interpret imaging findings clearly, ensuring treatment decisions are guided by direct visual evidence of joint inflammation and structural change.

Ines Varga

Rheumatology nurse specialist

Ines Varga serves as our rheumatology nurse specialist and manages the dedicated named-nurse telephone line for registered clinic patients. She provides practical education on medication schedules, monitors routine laboratory results, and assists patients through symptom changes between formal reviews. Ines works closely with individuals during their four, twelve, and twenty-four week follow-ups, serving as a dependable, continuous point of clinical contact throughout their long-term care at our clinic.

Tamsin Rehn

Physiotherapist

Tamsin Rehn is our clinic physiotherapist, working with patients to preserve joint movement, build muscular stability, and ease morning stiffness. She conducts individualized forty-five minute physiotherapy sessions at 12 Linden Row, teaching practical hand exercises, stretching protocols, and joint-protection techniques. Tamsin coordinates directly with our medical team to align physical rehabilitation milestones with each patient's one-page written management plan, helping patients stay active and confident.

Leila Osei

Occupational therapist

Leila Osei is our occupational therapist specializing in hand splinting, joint ergonomics, and workplace functional assessments. She evaluates how joint stiffness impacts daily tasks such as writing, typing, and manual work, providing custom-fitted splints and assistive strategies. Leila works alongside our rheumatologists to adapt everyday routines, helping patients maintain professional and household independence while protecting inflamed joints from unnecessary physical strain and fatigue.

Samir Haddad

Pharmacist liaison

Samir Haddad is our pharmacist liaison, responsible for conducting structured medicines reviews and coordinating prescription safety. He assesses potential drug interactions, explains disease-modifying antirheumatic therapies, and ensures patients understand routine blood monitoring requirements. Samir collaborates with community pharmacies across Harrow Quay and our consulting doctors to ensure repeat prescriptions and medication adjustments proceed smoothly, safely, and without administrative delays.

Ruth Calloway

Reception and scheduling lead

Ruth Calloway leads our reception and patient scheduling desk at 12 Linden Row. She manages initial appointment bookings, coordinates the printable morning stiffness diary distribution, and organizes early morning flare-day slots by telephone. Ruth ensures that all clinic visits, follow-up reviews, and diagnostic sessions run punctually, welcoming patients warmly and maintaining clear communication across our entire clinical schedule each week.

pages.title: Fees
pages.content:
Fees

FEES AND RECEIPTS

Home / Fees

Fees

We provide clear, transparent pricing for all diagnostic consultations, ultrasound examinations, and therapeutic treatments at Yawara Rheumatology. All clinic fees were reviewed on 2026.04.01.

Fees reviewed 2026.04.01

The one-page written plan is included in the first consultation. Receipts are issued for insurers on the day.

Consultation and review fees

Our initial consultation fee is €140 for a comprehensive sixty-minute appointment, which includes a complete clinical history, twenty-eight joint examination, bedside joint ultrasound, and blood sampling on the day. Follow-up reviews are priced at €75 for a thirty-minute appointment, covering repeat joint counts and treatment evaluation. Every patient receives a signed one-page written management plan following their initial assessment at no additional charge, ensuring full transparency without unexpected administrative fees.

Ultrasound and procedural fees

Standalone joint ultrasound sessions of twenty minutes are priced at €90 for targeted assessment of specific joint structures. Therapeutic joint injections are provided at €110 per joint, delivered under sterile conditions by experienced clinicians to relieve localized inflammation. Infusion monitoring visits are available at €55, covering dedicated nursing observation and vital sign checks during intravenous therapy, with the prescribed medicine billed separately.

Therapy sessions and receipt documentation

Individual physiotherapy sessions with Tamsin Rehn are priced at €65 for forty-five minutes of tailored joint rehabilitation and exercise instruction. We provide itemized receipts following every appointment, detailing all clinical codes and professional services rendered. While we operate on a direct fee basis, these receipts can be submitted to private health insurance providers for potential reimbursement depending on your specific policy coverage and insurance terms.

pages.title: Questions
pages.content:
Questions

ASKED OFTEN

Home / Questions

Questions

Here you will find clear answers to common questions regarding our clinical consultations, appointment scheduling, and treatment protocols. If your question is not covered below, our team is available by telephone.

Hand splints

OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY

Do I need a formal referral from my doctor to book an appointment?

You do not require a formal doctor's referral to schedule a first consultation at Yawara Rheumatology. While many patients are referred directly by family physicians or physiotherapists across Harrow Quay, self-referrals are welcome. When you contact reception, we will provide our seven-day morning stiffness diary sheet to complete before your visit. If you have recent blood test results or clinical hospital letters, please bring them along to your appointment.

How do the morning flare-day slots work?

Morning flare-day slots are reserved specifically for registered clinic patients experiencing sudden, acute joint inflammation. These appointments take place on weekdays between 8:30 and 9:30, and on Saturdays between 8:30 and 9:00. To access a flare slot, call our reception desk at +1 555 0142 300 at 8:30 on the morning you require evaluation. We will assess your symptoms and arrange a same-morning clinical appointment with our team.

Are joint injections available during my appointment?

Joint injections are available at €110 per joint when clinically indicated to treat localized swelling and pain. Dr. Miriam Achterberg or Dr. Kofi Mensah-Lund evaluates the target joint using ultrasound to ensure accurate needle placement. Injections may be performed during your consultation if appropriate or scheduled as a dedicated follow-up procedure. Your clinician will discuss the expected clinical benefits, potential discomfort, and aftercare before proceeding with any injection.

How is pregnancy planning managed for rheumatology patients?

Rheumatic conditions and disease-modifying medications require careful review prior to conception. If you are planning a pregnancy, we review your current prescriptions to confirm safety and adjust therapies that are contraindicated during pregnancy. For comprehensive obstetric monitoring alongside rheumatology care, we refer patients to specialized maternal-fetal medicine units while continuing to coordinate joint disease management throughout your pregnancy and postpartum period to support your joint health.

Can the clinic provide sick notes for my workplace?

Yes, our consulting rheumatologists can issue medical certificates and workplace fitness notes when active joint inflammation prevents you from working. We can document specific functional limitations, such as restricted typing, lifting limitations, or reduced standing capacity during severe flare periods. In addition, our occupational therapist Leila Osei can recommend workplace adjustments and ergonomic aids to help you safely resume your professional duties as symptoms stabilize.

What should I bring to my first consultation?

Please bring your completed seven-day morning stiffness diary sheet, which records your waking symptoms over the preceding week. You should also bring a current list of all prescription medications and nutritional supplements you take. If you possess previous laboratory blood results, imaging reports, or hospital correspondence, bring physical copies to assist your doctor during the sixty-minute assessment, ensuring a comprehensive clinical review.

How does the named nurse contact line work?

Every registered patient is assigned a named nurse contact line managed by our rheumatology nurse specialist, Ines Varga. This telephone service provides support for medication queries, side-effect questions, and routine laboratory monitoring between scheduled appointments. Calls are returned during our regular clinic hours, ensuring you receive direct clinical guidance from a professional who knows your medical history without needing to book an unscheduled consultation.

When are routine follow-up reviews scheduled?

Following your initial plan meeting, standard follow-up reviews are scheduled at four, twelve, and twenty-four weeks to monitor treatment response and medication tolerance. Each review includes a standardized twenty-eight joint count and symptom reassessment. Once your condition stabilizes on an established treatment plan, follow-up reviews transition to a regular schedule of once every three months, maintaining consistent clinical oversight across the year.

+1 555 0142 300

pages.title: Notices
pages.content:
Notices

SIGN UP

Home / Notices

Notices

Register your email address to receive direct operational updates, schedule changes, and clinic publications from Yawara Rheumatology. We send concise, relevant notices without unnecessary promotional messaging.

Stay informed on clinic hours and holiday schedules

Subscribing to our clinic notices ensures you receive timely notifications regarding planned changes to our operating hours at 12 Linden Row. We notify registered subscribers well in advance of upcoming public holiday closures, revised Saturday consulting times, and seasonal scheduling adjustments. This service helps you plan routine prescription renewals and review visits without encountering unexpected clinic closures or unnecessary scheduling conflicts.

2026.11.04 Flare-day slots now open at 8:30

Your mail program opens with a request addressed to the clinic. It is not a subscription until the clinic confirms it.

Request notices by email

Updates on flare-day slot availability

Registered patients can opt to receive practical announcements regarding morning flare-day slot arrangements. We share procedural updates on how early morning telephone bookings operate for our weekday 8:30 to 9:30 slots and Saturday 8:30 to 9:00 appointments. Receiving these updates ensures you remain fully informed on how to secure same-day clinical assessment when experiencing sudden joint inflammation, avoiding confusion during active symptom flares.

New journal articles and patient notes

Subscribers can also select our journal digest to receive newly published patient case notes, clinical articles, and rheumatology educational guides. Our writings explain diagnostic procedures, joint ultrasound techniques, and practical strategies for managing morning stiffness at home and in the workplace. You can adjust your subscription preferences or unsubscribe at any time through our reception desk, keeping complete control over the communications you receive.

pages.title: Contact
pages.content:
12 Linden Row / Entrance

Contact

FIND US

Home / Contact

Contact

Yawara Rheumatology is located on the second floor of 12 Linden Row in Harrow Quay, with full lift access. We welcome inquiries by telephone or through our online contact form.

Clinic location and transport access

Our consulting rooms are situated at 12 Linden Row, Harrow Quay, on the second floor with step-free lift access from street level. For patients arriving by public transport, Bus 14 stops at the Linden Row bus stop, which is located just a three-minute level walk from our clinic entrance. The building entrance features automatic glass doors and an accessible passenger lift to reach our reception area comfortably.

Opening hours and telephone inquiries

Our reception desk and telephone lines at +1 555 0142 300 are open Monday to Friday from 8:30 to 17:30, and on Saturdays from 8:30 to 12:30. The clinic is closed on Sundays and public holidays. Dedicated morning flare-day slots operate on weekdays between 8:30 and 9:30, and on Saturdays between 8:30 and 9:00 for registered patients requiring same-day review by our clinical team.

+1 555 0142 300

Mon–Fri 8:30–17:30 · Sat 8:30–12:30 · Closed Sun & public holidays

Online message inquiries

To request an initial consultation or ask general administrative questions, you may submit our online contact form. Please provide your full name, telephone number, email address, preferred appointment day, and a general message. To protect your personal privacy, please do not include confidential medical details or sensitive health histories in this form. Our reception team will contact you by telephone to confirm arrangements and answer administrative queries.

Email the clinic

pages.title: Privacy
pages.content:
Home / Privacy

Privacy

This privacy policy outlines how Yawara Rheumatology collects, stores, and protects your personal and administrative data. We handle all information in strict accordance with professional confidentiality standards.

Information collected through our website

When you use our website or contact form, we collect administrative contact details including your name, telephone number, email address, and scheduling preferences. We explicitly advise visitors not to submit detailed clinical histories through unsecured web forms. In addition, when you subscribe to clinic notices, we store your email address solely to deliver requested updates regarding clinic hours, flare-day arrangements, and published journal articles to your inbox.

Use and protection of administrative data

Administrative information submitted through this website is used exclusively to respond to inquiries, coordinate appointments at 12 Linden Row, and deliver subscribed communications. We do not sell, rent, or disclose personal contact details to third parties or marketing organizations. All electronic records are maintained on secure servers protected by industry-standard technical safeguards, and access is restricted to authorized clinic staff who require it for scheduling.

Your data protection rights

You retain full rights to request access to the personal contact information we hold about you, request corrections to inaccurate records, or ask for the deletion of your contact details from our notice mailing lists. To exercise any of these rights, please contact our reception team by telephone at +1 555 0142 300 or speak with our staff in person at the clinic during regular opening hours.

posts.title: The knuckle that stiffened overnight
posts.excerpt: Ana, a thirty-eight-year-old cellist, records how tracking her morning stiffness led to a structured sixty-minute diagnostic consultation at Yawara Rheumatology.
posts.content:
When thirty-eight-year-old cellist Ana woke on a damp Tuesday morning, her left middle knuckle felt abnormally thick and rigid. Placing her fingers across the fingerboard of her cello, she noticed that shifting into third position caused a dull, dragging resistance that had never been there before. By midday, after several hours of warm tea and gentle movement, the tightness had eased enough for her to rehearse, but the following morning the stiffness returned, this time accompanied by visible swelling across the proximal interphalangeal joint. Recognizing that joint inflammation could threaten her musical livelihood, she contacted Yawara Rheumatology at 12 Linden Row in Harrow Quay.

Rather than scheduling an immediate hurried review, our reception desk registered Ana's details and provided our printable seven-day morning stiffness diary sheet. For one complete week, Ana kept the diary sheet on her bedside table next to a pencil. Each morning upon waking at seven, she recorded the exact duration of her joint stiffness, noting down how long it took before her fingers could flex comfortably around a coffee mug. She tracked which specific joints felt warm to touch, noting persistent swelling in her left middle knuckle and subtle puffiness in both wrists. When her sixty-minute appointment arrived the following Monday at 8:30, she brought seven days of clear, objective observations rather than vague recollections.

Ana's first consultation was conducted by lead rheumatologist Dr. Miriam Achterberg. The sixty-minute session began with an unhurried discussion of Ana's musical schedule, daily physical demands, and family medical background. Dr. Achterberg then conducted a standardized twenty-eight joint examination, methodically checking both hands, wrists, elbows, shoulders, knees, and ankles for signs of tenderness, swelling, and fluid accumulation. While Ana had primarily noticed her left finger, the systematic examination detected mild, early warmth in her right wrist as well, underscoring the importance of examining twenty-eight distinct joints rather than focusing solely on the joint that prompted the call.

Next, bedside musculoskeletal ultrasound was performed directly in the consulting room. Dr. Achterberg applied acoustic gel to Ana's affected knuckles and wrists, placing the ultrasound probe flat against the joint line. On the monitor, they could clearly observe the distinction between healthy tissue and thickened synovial lining, confirming active local inflammation. Before Ana left the clinic, routine blood samples were drawn on-site to measure inflammatory markers and specific autoantibodies, completing all essential diagnostic investigations in a single morning visit.

Eight days later, Ana returned to 12 Linden Row for her dedicated plan meeting. Together with Dr. Achterberg and rheumatology nurse specialist Ines Varga, she reviewed the laboratory results, ultrasound imagery, and physical joint scores. The team formulated a one-page written management plan summarizing her working diagnosis, prescribed medical therapy, tailored hand exercises designed by physiotherapist Tamsin Rehn, and scheduled review milestones. Both Ana and Dr. Achterberg signed the sheet, and Ana received a physical copy to keep at home.

Under this agreed plan, Ana's ongoing care was structured around regular clinical check-ups at four, twelve, and twenty-four weeks, moving to three-month intervals once her joint inflammation stabilized. Between visits, she was given access to the clinic's named-nurse telephone line with Ines Varga for any questions regarding prescription adjustments or symptom fluctuations. By following a clear, measured process from symptom diary to written plan, Ana established a predictable framework for protecting her joints and maintaining her music.

posts.title: Planning around a flare week
posts.excerpt: Peter, 61, a bus driver, how the flare-day slot and nurse line work.
posts.content:
Peter drives the number 14. When his wrists flare he cannot grip the wheel for the first hour, and a week of that is a problem for him and for his passengers.

His plan says what to do: phone at 8:30 for a flare-day slot, and speak to his named nurse, Ines, about adjusting medicine within the limits the plan sets.

He says the page on his fridge matters more than any single appointment. He knows who to call and what will be asked.

posts.title: What the twelve-week review is for
posts.excerpt: Hana, 45, a teacher, what is checked and why.
posts.content:
By week twelve there is enough history to see a pattern. Hana’s review started with her diary, then the same 28 joints that were examined at the first visit.

Bloods and, where useful, a repeat ultrasound show whether inflammation has settled. Her plan was adjusted, and the next review date was written on the page before she left.

Reviews at 4, 12 and 24 weeks are the early rhythm; after that, every three months.
